title: Copilot Studio: labelled and encrypted file uploads for agents on the Microsoft 365 channel
summary: Hold: the blanket statement that none of the listed controls is confirmed for these uploads understates Microsoft's documented monitoring coverage for Copilot Studio agent interactions. The roadmap facts and revised credit rates are supported; the DLP and label-permissions routes also need small clarifications about reaching the actual rule or permissions.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans labelled-file upload support for Copilot Studio agents deployed on the Microsoft 365 channel; the description names no other channel.
claims.quote: Unblock users from upload files with Microsoft Purview Information Protection (MPIP) sensitivity labels to Copilot Studio agents deployed on the M365 channel.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The roadmap describes content processing based on the user's or agent's account permissions.
claims.quote: With this support agents can process content based on the user's/agents account permissions

claims.claim: The roadmap plans end-to-end enforcement of label protections.
claims.quote: with label protections enforced end-to-end.

claims.claim: A Learn page describing the planned labelled-upload feature and its detailed behaviour was not found at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Purview sensitivity labelled encrypted file uploads 571305 File uploads default API EXTRACT. Read Allow file input from users, ai-copilot-studio and SharePoint knowledge troubleshooting; found current restrictions, not the planned support.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The existing file-input documentation says encrypted files, including sensitivity-labelled or password-protected files, are unsupported.
claims.quote: Files with encryption, such as sensitivity labels or password protection, aren't supported.

claims.claim: For an encrypted or password-protected Office upload, the agent tells the user that it cannot read the file.
claims.quote: When a user uploads a password-protected or encrypted Office file, the agent tells the user that the file is encrypted or password-protected and can't be read.

claims.claim: Some rights-managed or label-encrypted uploads instead produce a generic error.
claims.quote: For some rights-managed or label-encrypted files, the agent returns a generic error instead.

claims.claim: The cited file-input article describes agents powered by the standard harness.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: The file-input page points users to Microsoft Copilot Chat, which supports sensitivity-labelled files.
claims.quote: or use a Microsoft 365 experience such as Microsoft Copilot Chat, which supports sensitivity-labeled files.

claims.claim: Connecting an agent to the Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels makes it available for chat in Teams and Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: After you publish your agent at least once, you can connect it to the Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels so users can chat with it in both Teams and Microsoft Copilot.

claims.claim: The documented AI protection model requires VIEW for a user to receive data encrypted by a sensitivity label.
claims.quote: When the sensitivity label applies encryption, users must have the EXTRACT usage right, as well as VIEW, for the AI apps to return the data.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The documented Copilot protection model uses the user's effective EXTRACT right to determine whether encrypted content can be displayed.
claims.quote: It's this usage right that determines whether Copilot or agents can display text to the user from encrypted content.

claims.claim: The Purview Copilot Studio page documents encryption support only with sensitivity labels and only for a SharePoint knowledge source.
claims.quote: Encryption is supported only with sensitivity labels, and only for the SharePoint knowledge source.

claims.claim: The cited SharePoint troubleshooting page instead says agents cannot extract or ground on content whose protection encrypts the file.
claims.quote: However, the agent can't extract or ground on content whose protection encrypts the file. This limitation includes sensitivity labels that apply encryption, Double Key Encryption (DKE), and password-protected files.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[3].note
claims.claim: The person applying encryption is the Rights Management owner and always retains EXTRACT.
claims.quote: The person applying the encryption always has the EXTRACT usage right, because they are the Rights Management owner.

claims.claim: Full control (OWNER) includes EXTRACT.
claims.quote: Because the Full control (OWNER) usage right includes all the usage rights, EXTRACT is automatically included with Full control.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Agent flows, connectors and tools can pass user-uploaded files to downstream services, including SharePoint and ServiceNow.
claims.quote: Optionally, you can add logic in your flow to send this file to SharePoint, ServiceNow, Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and similar services.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a sensitivity-label check at the uploaded-file hand-off to these flows or tools.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio uploaded files flows tools connector sensitivity label protection check DLP. Read Pass files to agent flows, connectors, and tools, Allow file input from users and ai-copilot-studio; none documents a label check at that hand-off.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The planned labelled-upload identity model is not documented beyond the roadmap's account-permissions wording.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio sensitivity labelled file upload support M365 channel default prerequisites EXTRACT permissions identity. Read the roadmap, file-input article and ai-copilot-studio; no detailed identity model for the planned support was found.

claims.claim: Copilot and agents have documented restrictions on unopened SharePoint and OneDrive files encrypted with user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: Copilot and agents can't access unopened documents in SharePoint and OneDrive when they're labeled and encrypted with user-defined permissions

claims.claim: A default sensitivity label extending SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents is an exception to that unopened-file restriction.
claims.quote: unless the label is used as a default sensitivity label that extends SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents

claims.claim: Directly referencing a file by typing '/' is another exception to that unopened-file restriction.
claims.quote: or they're directly referenced by typing "/"

claims.claim: Both exceptions require the user to have EXTRACT.
claims.quote: (and in both cases, the user has EXTRACT permissions).

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Label-based DLP at the Microsoft 365 Copilot location is documented for Copilot Studio agents with a SharePoint knowledge source.
claims.quote: When the knowledge source is SharePoint, a DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can restrict agents built in Copilot Studio for Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 Copilot from processing sensitive content based on a specified sensitivity label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: DLP does not scan the contents of files uploaded directly into Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts.
claims.quote: DLP can't scan the contents of files that you upload directly into prompts, so evaluation of the uploaded file for sensitive data doesn't occur. DLP only checks the text you type into the prompt itself.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Label-based Copilot DLP coverage of the planned Copilot Studio labelled uploads is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio uploaded files flows tools connector sensitivity label protection check DLP. Read ai-copilot-studio and the Copilot DLP location page. The former limits agent coverage to SharePoint knowledge sources; the latter excludes scanning files uploaded directly into prompts.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Ordinary Copilot Studio agent usage is measured and billed in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are the unit that measures agent usage. You calculate the total cost based on the sum of the Copilot Credits your organization uses.

claims.claim: Copilot Credits measure the time and effort needed to retrieve information, respond to prompts and use actions.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits measure the time and effort your agent needs to retrieve information, respond to prompts, and use any actions or custom Azure Bot Service skills.

claims.claim: The base feature rate for a generative answer is 2 Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: | Generative answer^2^ | 2 Copilot Credits | No charge |

claims.claim: The Text and generative AI tools (premium) reasoning-model meter charges 10 Copilot Credits per 1,000 billed tokens.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are calculated from the exact number of billed tokens, at 10 Copilot Credits per 1,000 tokens.

claims.claim: When a generative answer uses a reasoning model, the premium token meter is additional to the generative-answer feature rate.
claims.quote: Total cost = feature rate for generative answers + text and generative AI tools (premium) per 1000 tokens.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Classic answers, generative answers and tenant graph grounding in Copilot Chat, Teams or SharePoint are not charged for a Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed user when the agent uses that user's authenticated identity.
claims.quote: If you have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, using agents in Copilot Chat, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint for classic answers, generative answers, or Microsoft Graph tenant grounding isn't charged when the agent runs with your authenticated identity.

claims.claim: The existing File uploads setting is maker-side and configured for an individual agent.
claims.quote: Makers can allow users of their agent to upload files during chat interactions with their agent. 1. Go to the Settings page for your agent, and select Generative AI.

Read Allow file input from users; it documents the current setting, not its future interaction.

claims.claim: Existing file input is configured in Copilot Studio through Settings > Generative AI > File processing capabilities > File uploads.
claims.quote: 1. Go to the Settings page for your agent, and select Generative AI. 2. Navigate to the File processing capabilities section. 3. Turn on File uploads.

claims.claim: An automation operation and deciding property for the existing File uploads setting are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio File uploads setting API Dataverse botconfiguration botcomponent file processing pac admin PowerShell. Read bot entity and pac copilot references: generic configuration updates exist, but no deciding file-upload property is documented.

claims.claim: The printed Purview route correctly reaches the Copilot DLP policy location, but stops before configuring the sensitivity-label rule.
claims.quote: Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy. Select the Custom template, then Custom policy. On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
claims.fix: Keep the printed route to the location and append to controls[2].note: 'After selecting the location, add a rule with Content contains > Sensitivity labels and set the action to Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content.' This completes the documented route to the rule without inventing intervening wizard labels; see https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-learn-about.

claims.claim: New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name <name> -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @('CopilotExperiences') creates the Copilot DLP policy using the documented location variable.
claims.quote: New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name "Copilot Policy" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences")

claims.claim: New-DLPComplianceRule with Name, Policy, AdvancedRule and the printed ExcludeContentProcessing/Block RestrictAccess value configures the label-based content-processing restriction.
claims.quote: New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The printed label-edit route correctly reaches Access control but stops before selecting the permission settings.
claims.quote: Follow the general instructions to create or edit a sensitivity label and make sure the Files & other data assets option is selected for the label's scope
claims.fix: Extend controls[3].ui.path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > label > Edit label > Define the scope for this label > Files & other data assets > Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected > Control access > Access control > Configure access control settings > Assign permissions now > Assign permissions > Choose permissions'. The existing note can identify Copy and extract content(EXTRACT). The opening route is documented at the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels and the remaining steps at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels; selecting the users or groups is the scope choice.

claims.claim: Set-Label with EncryptionEnabled $true, EncryptionProtectionType Template and EncryptionRightsDefinitions changes the identified label's template encryption and user rights.
claims.quote: The EncryptionRightsDefinitions parameter specifies the rights users have when accessing protected. This parameter uses the syntax Identity1:Rights1,Rights2;Identity2:Rights3,Rights4.

claims.claim: On Access control, Configure access control settings enables configuration and Assign permissions now selects administrator-defined permissions.
claims.quote: When you select Configure access control settings on the Access control page to create or edit a sensitivity label, choose one of the following options: Assign permissions now

claims.claim: The Purview portal displays EXTRACT as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, the EXTRACT usage right is displayed as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).

claims.claim: Sensitivity-label integration for SharePoint and OneDrive can be enabled in Purview through Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Turn on now.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels. If you see a message to turn on the ability to process content in Office online files, select Turn on now

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true enables sensitivity-label integration for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: To enable the new capabilities, use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the EnableAIPIntegration parameter: Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true

claims.claim: The portal method of enabling SharePoint and OneDrive sensitivity labels requires a global administrator.
claims.quote: You must sign in as a global administrator for your tenant.

claims.claim: Multi-Geo tenants must use PowerShell to enable sensitivity-label integration for all geo-locations.
claims.quote: If you have Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo, you must use PowerShell to enable these capabilities for all your geo-locations.

claims.claim: The Copilot experiences & agents summary report is reached through Purview Solutions > DSPM for AI (classic) > Reports > Copilot experiences & agents.
claims.quote: Wait at least a day for data, and then navigate to the Reports page to view the results of your policy. Select Copilot experiences & agents

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation for the DSPM for AI classic Copilot experiences & agents summary report itself was found.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises waiting at least a day for policy data before viewing the report.
claims.quote: Wait at least a day for data, and then navigate to the Reports page to view the results of your policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that any of the listed controls governs the planned labelled uploads.
claims.quote: Use the following sections to identify the Microsoft Purview capabilities that are supported for AI interactions with agents built in Microsoft Copilot Studio
claims.fix: Replace 'Microsoft has not confirmed that any of them governs the planned labelled uploads' with 'Microsoft documents DSPM for AI (classic) reporting for AI interactions with agents built in Copilot Studio; upload-specific label enforcement and label-based DLP coverage are not yet documented.' The report row is within that documented agent-interaction reach, not an unconfirmed control. Keep the subsequent DLP limitations. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-copilot-studio.

claims.claim: Purview Data Security AI Admin is among the roles permitted to create or edit DLP policies for the Copilot location.
claims.quote: Purview Data Security AI Admin - Role for editing Data Loss Prevention policies related to Copilot and viewing AI content in Data Security Posture Management.
